'''Omri Moshe Sarig''' (Hebrew: עמרי משה שריג) is an Israeli mathematician specializing in ergodic theory and dynamical systems. He is a professor at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]], where he holds the Theodore R. and Edlyn Racoosin Professorial Chair in Mathematics.<ref name=weizmann>{{cite web |title=Omri Sarig – Faculty Profile |url=https://www.weizmann.ac.il/math/sarigo/home |website=Weizmann Institute of Science |date=18 July 2016 |access-date=14 September 2025}}</ref> Sarig is known for his contributions to thermodynamic formalism, symbolic dynamics, and the use of transfer operators in non-uniformly hyperbolic dynamics.

== Career ==
Sarig earned his Ph.D. in mathematics from [[Tel Aviv University]] in 2001.<ref name=weizmann/> His doctoral dissertation, ''Thermodynamic Formalism for Countable Markov Shifts'', was supervised by [[Jon Aaronson]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mathematics Genealogy Project – Omri Sarig |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=103445 |website=Mathematics Genealogy Project |access-date=14 September 2025}}</ref>

From 2000 to 2003, he was the Warwick Zeeman Lecturer at the [[University of Warwick]].<ref name=weizmann/> He then joined [[Pennsylvania State University]], serving first as an assistant professor (2003–2006) and later as an associate professor (2006–2011).<ref name=weizmann/>

In 2006, Sarig moved to the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]], where he became associate professor in 2009 and full professor in 2014.<ref name=weizmann/> He served as Head of the Department of Mathematics from 2014 to 2018.<ref name=weizmann/>

== Research ==
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=October 2025}}
Sarig has developed methods using transfer operators to study countable Markov shifts and symbolic dynamics in smooth ergodic theory. His research also includes results on horocycle flows and multifractal analysis.

== Honors and awards ==
* [[Michael Brin Prize in Dynamical Systems]] (2013), "for his work on the thermodynamics of countable Markov shifts and his Markov partition for surface diffeomorphisms with positive topological entropy".<ref>{{cite web |title=Michael Brin Prize in Dynamical Systems |url=https://science.psu.edu/math/research/dynsys/brinprize |website=Pennsylvania State University Department of Mathematics |access-date=14 September 2025}}</ref>
* [[Erdős Prize]] (2013), awarded by the Israel Mathematical Union.<ref>{{cite web |title=Anna and Lajos Erdős Prize |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Honours/Anna_and_Lajos_Erdos_Prize/ |website=MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive |publisher=University of St Andrews |access-date=14 September 2025}}</ref>
* [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] (2006).<ref>{{cite web |title=2006 Annual Report |url=https://sloan.org/storage/app/media/files/annual_reports/2006_annual_report.pdf |website=Alfred P. Sloan Foundation |date=2006 |access-date=14 September 2025}}</ref>
* Invited Speaker, [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] (Hyderabad, 2010) in the section "Dynamical Systems and Ordinary Differential Equations".<ref>{{cite web |title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers – Omri Sarig |url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=Sarig |website=International Mathematical Union |access-date=14 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=ICM 2010 – Lecture Abstract: Omri Sarig |url=https://intlpress.com/site/pub/files/preview/bookpubs/00000746.pdf |publisher=International Press |date=2010 |access-date=14 September 2025}}</ref>
